// NOTE: This is an example tools configuration file showing all available options with detailed comments
// USAGE: Copy to tools.json and fill in your actual values
// ToolExecutionMode: Execute tools sequentially or in parallel (Sequential or Parallel)
// Servers: List of MCP (Model Context Protocol) server configurations

Servers.// Name: Unique identifier for the MCP server
Servers.Name: todo-list
Servers.// Command: Command to start the MCP server (e.g., npx, node, python, path to executable)
Servers.// Args: Array of command-line arguments for the server
Servers.// Env: Optional environment variables for the server process (augments/overwrites inherited environment)
Servers.// Note: Set a variable to null to remove it from the inherited environment

Servers.// Example: Another MCP server with custom environment variables
Servers.Name: custom-server

Env.// Description: Environment variables are set when starting the server process (not per tool call)

Servers.// Example: Local binary/executable file (Windows .exe, Linux binary, etc.)
Servers.// IMPORTANT: Use FULL ABSOLUTE PATH to the executable in the Command field
Servers.// Note: On Windows, use double backslashes (\\) or forward slashes (/) in paths
Servers.Name: local-tool

Env.// Description: Environment variables for the local executable

Servers.// Example: Python MCP server using full path to python.exe
Servers.// Tip: Useful when you have multiple Python versions or virtual environments
Servers.Name: python-tool

// AutoDiscoverTools: Automatically discover tools from MCP servers on startup (default: true)
// ToolExecutionTimeoutSeconds: Maximum time in seconds to wait for a tool to execute (default: 180)
// MaxToolCallDepth: Maximum depth of nested tool calls to prevent infinite loops (1-50, default: 10)
